sources.title: Monogamy relations for symmetric multiqubit systems
sources.authors: Eduardo Serrano-Ensástiga, Olivier Giraud and John Martin
sources.summary: Tables I–III, Appendix A and Theorem 1 supply the symmetric-sector bounds, representative states and the nine-qubit eighth-sector result. Table III includes conjectural optima as well as established results.
sources.notes: The supplied working draft distinguishes conjectural entries in Appendix A and contains unresolved [?] references. The follow-up located a pinned public threshold supplement and independently checked the relevant constructions. Remaining gaps and the status of every entry are documented in the research notes.

sources.title: Multiqubit monogamy relations beyond shadow inequalities
sources.authors: Eduardo Serrano-Ensástiga, Olivier Giraud, John Martin
sources.summary: Defines Pauli sector lengths and proves bounds for general pure multiqubit states. Bounds attained by symmetric product, GHZ or tetrahedron states also certify extrema within the symmetric subspace.
sources.notes: Table I concerns all pure states, not only symmetric states. Its AME, tensor-product and generic computational-basis witnesses must not be imported as symmetric examples. Gray cells denote proven optima; unshaded cells are conjectured numerical optima.

sources.title: Universality in fidelity-based quantum metrology
sources.authors: Luis Aragón-Muñoz, Chryssomalis Chryssomalakos, Ana Gabriela Flores-Delgado, John Martin, Eduardo Serrano-Ensástiga
sources.summary: Expresses orientation-averaged sensing objectives using SU(2)-invariant vectors. Explains why extremal sensing states lie on the boundary of the invariant locus.
sources.notes: Its invariants r_l are multipole quantities. Optimal average fidelity or QFI does not automatically imply an extremum of any individual Pauli sector S_k.

sources.title: Multiqubit symmetric states with high geometric entanglement
sources.authors: J. Martin, O. Giraud, P. A. Braun, D. Braun, T. Bastin
sources.summary: Introduces useful Dicke-basis and Majorana descriptions, and identifies highly geometrically entangled configurations, including tetrahedral and octahedral states.
sources.notes: The optimization objective is geometric entanglement, not sector length. The five-qubit square-pyramid optimum in this paper is not interchangeable with a triangular-bipyramid or a sector-length optimizer.

sources.title: Multiqubit symmetric states with maximally mixed one-qubit reductions
sources.authors: D. Baguette, T. Bastin, J. Martin
sources.summary: Characterizes symmetric states with maximally mixed one-qubit reductions through Dicke coefficients and vanishing collective spin. Provides an explicit four-qubit family containing GHZ and tetrahedron states.
sources.notes: Equations (8)–(13) identify states with S1=0 using the catalogue normalization. Higher-order reductions are maximally mixed only within the symmetric subspace, not the full qubit Hilbert space.

sources.title: Anticoherence of spin states with point-group symmetries
sources.authors: D. Baguette, F. Damanet, O. Giraud, J. Martin
sources.summary: Relates point-group symmetries of Majorana constellations to anticoherence, supplies low-qubit constructions, and proves existence of anticoherent states of arbitrary order for sufficiently large spins.
sources.notes: Useful for representative states and symmetry labels. A point-group name alone is insufficient to certify a sector-length optimum. Spin convention: |D_N^(k)> corresponds to |N/2,N/2-k>.

sources.title: Anticoherence measures for pure spin states
sources.summary: Defines purity-based anticoherence A_t=(t+1)(1−Tr rho_t^2)/t, gives explicit cat and tetrahedron states, and studies the existence of states with degenerate Majorana constellations.
sources.notes: A_t concerns the entire reduced-state purity, a weighted combination of sector lengths. Maximizing A_t is generally different from minimizing S_t alone.

sources.title: Entanglement robustness against particle loss in multiqubit systems
sources.authors: A. Neven, J. Martin, T. Bastin
sources.summary: Characterizes pure entangled states that lose all entanglement after losing one qubit and relates symmetric-state robustness to SLOCC classes.
sources.notes: Supports physical descriptions of GHZ and Dicke families, not new individual sector-length extrema. Corollary 2 on page 3 characterizes fragile symmetric states.

sources.title: Tensor Representation of Spin States
sources.authors: O. Giraud, D. Braun, D. Baguette, T. Bastin, J. Martin
sources.summary: Builds spin operators by projecting Pauli strings onto the symmetric subspace and characterizes anticoherence through maximally mixed reduced states and vanishing multipoles.
sources.notes: Theorem 1 (page 3): projected Pauli operators. Theorem 3 (page 4): t-anticoherence iff rho_t=I_(t+1)/(t+1). Corollary 1 (page 5): equivalent multipole criterion.

sources.title: Extreme depolarization for any spin
sources.summary: Provides a spin-to-symmetric-qubit dictionary and explicit highly anticoherent states, and relates isotropic and anisotropic depolarization to entanglement and multipole structure.
sources.notes: Table II (page 4) defines GHZ, balanced Dicke and W states; Table IV (page 17) lists explicit highest-order anticoherent examples. Fastest depolarization is a distinct optimization problem from extremizing S_k.

sources.title: Optimal Detection of Rotations about Unknown Axes by Coherent and Anticoherent States
sources.authors: John Martin, Stefan Weigert, Olivier Giraud
sources.summary: Writes average rotation fidelity in terms of anticoherence measures and gives explicit low-spin candidate states, including the tetrahedron, triangular bipyramid and octahedron.
sources.notes: The local PDF is the accepted version dated June 16; journal publication and DOI verified as June 22. The metrological optimum depends on rotation angle and should not be imported as a sector-length optimum without a separate proof.

constructions.title: Coherent product states
constructions.text: The symmetric product state and every collective rotation of it have a binomial sector profile. It attains the full-sector minimum and the low-sector maxima whenever the cited upper bound applies. In particular, $\max S_5=\binom n5$ for every $n\ge10$, now supported by an exact spectral certificate.

constructions.title: GHZ states
constructions.text: For $k<n$, odd sectors vanish and even sectors equal $\binom nk$. The full-sector value is $2^{n-1}$ for odd $n$ and $2^{n-1}+1$ for even $n$. These states attain all proper odd-sector minima and every full-sector maximum.

constructions.title: Dicke states
constructions.text: The normalized equal superposition of bit strings with $q$ excitations. The $q=1$ case is the W state; $q=n/2$ is the balanced Dicke state for even $n$. Individual Dicke representatives appear throughout the table.

constructions.title: Tetrahedral and octahedral states
constructions.text: The tetrahedral four-qubit state has sector vector $(0,2,8,5)$. The octahedral six-qubit state has $(0,5,0,35,0,23)$. Their Majorana symmetries provide useful analytic representatives; the table identifies the sectors for which optimality is established.

constructions.title: The even-sector lower bound
constructions.text: Every symmetric state obeys this lower bound for even $k$. Equality requires the even multipoles through order $k$ to vanish. Attainment must be checked separately for each size: a lower bound alone does not identify a minimizing pure state.

constructions.title: Anticoherence and related objectives
constructions.text: A $t$-anticoherent state has $\rho_t=I_{t+1}/(t+1)$ in the symmetric subspace. Purity-based anticoherence, geometric entanglement, mean rotation fidelity and depolarization probe related properties, but their optimizers need not extremize an individual $S_k$.

constructions.title: The exact fourth-sector maximum threshold
constructions.text: The proved eight-qubit upper bound extends by convexity and symmetric reduction to every larger size. Coherent product states attain it. The seven-qubit maximum is 265/7, strictly above 35, so the least eventual threshold is exactly eight.

definitions.title: Sector lengths: the sum convention
definitions.text: For a normalized pure state, sum the squared expectation values of all $n$-qubit Pauli strings of weight $k$. There is no division by $\binom nk$. Here $S_0=1$ and $\sum_{k=0}^nS_k=2^n$.

definitions.title: The symmetric subspace and basis
definitions.text: The search is over normalized pure states in $\operatorname{Sym}^n(\mathbb C^2)$, equivalently spin $j=n/2$. The Dicke index $r$ counts excitations. Downloaded amplitudes are ordered $r=0,\ldots,n$. Collective rotations preserve all sector lengths; a representative does not enumerate the entire equality set.

definitions.title: Reduced purities and numerical checks
definitions.text: For symmetric states, all $t$-qubit reductions have the same purity $r_t=\mathrm{Tr}(\rho_t^2)$. The inversion below computes sector lengths directly from Dicke coefficients. Numerical agreement checks attainment by the displayed state; it does not prove global optimality.
definitions.formula: r_t=2^{-t}\sum_{m=0}^{t}\frac{\binom tm}{\binom nm}S_m,\qquad S_m=\binom nm\sum_{t=0}^{m}(-1)^{m+t}2^t\binom mt r_t

definitions.title: Evidence and coverage
definitions.text: P: a global bound and an attaining symmetric state are supported by a cited source or an exact certificate. C: an exact attained candidate with no global proof. N: a numerically specified candidate. Exact value and proof status are separate. Every unresolved entry has a separate certified global bound. Values in cells may be rounded; downloads retain source expressions and amplitudes.

definitions.title: First-order anticoherence
definitions.text: The first sector vanishes precisely when the collective mean spin vanishes. With the purity-based measure $A_1=2(1-\mathrm{Tr}\rho_1^2)$, the following identity follows directly from the cited definitions.

definitions.title: Relation to the AME table
definitions.text: The browsing format is inspired by Felix Huber’s AME table. A maximally mixed symmetric reduction $I_{t+1}/(t+1)$ differs from the full $I_{2^t}/2^t$ reduction used in the AME condition for $t\ge2$. This catalogue concerns sector extrema of symmetric pure states.
